summary: community.crypto deprecated ansible-core 2.11 to 2.16 and cryptography < 3.4 (removed in 3.0.0), the no-op acme_certificate agreement and openssl_pkcs12 maciter_size options, the modify_account default of true, and the PyOpenSSL backend of openssl_pkcs12.
questions: Should I set modify_account in acme_certificate?
Is the agreement option in acme_certificate still needed?
What will the modify_account default change to?

answer_card.title: community.crypto deprecations
answer_card.answer_md:
- ansible-core 2.11 to 2.16 and **cryptography < 3.4** support deprecated, removed in community.crypto 3.0.0 (also drops Python < 3.7 on targets).
- `acme_certificate`: `agreement` has no effect and will be removed in 4.0.0.
- `acme_certificate`: `modify_account` default `true` will change to `false` in 4.0.0. Set it explicitly (preferably `false`) and use `community.crypto.acme_account` for account changes.
- `openssl_pkcs12`: `maciter_size` has no effect (removed in 4.0.0); the PyOpenSSL backend is removed in 3.0.0, after which cryptography 3.0+ is required.
